Physical journal entrusted to Donut Plains elder; chain of custody across eighty-five years unknown. Toadsmith filed one complete debrief through pre-Loyalist channels and went dark on approximately Day 21. Molly, Gus, and Vance returned safely. Toadsmith did not return with them. The crack in the wet concrete persisted for eighty-five years. The Loyalist movement grew from it. The truth is still emerging.
notableFeatures: Three-week timeline — the cover-up was under active construction when Toadsmith found the journal; the concrete was still wet; the crack he made has never healed

Bowser's performance dropping — when Toadsmith named the blade, the theatrics stopped, the smoke stopped, and Bowser went cold; this is the tell of a man who knows the blade is real and knows what its presence in a Regency investigation means
The SOS signal — sent to Regency backup, received by Eggman's forces; either intercepted or Eggman was already targeting the storage wing independently; both implications are alarming

Peach's journal — primary source written in her own hand, establishing coordination with the engineer as operational partner, the blade's Guild sourcing, the enemy's thirty-year proximity, and a final entry that reads as strategy rather than farewell

The engineer's three-week visibility — in the long historical view he is a shadow; three weeks after the assassination his gloves are on camera, his insignia is on the helicopter, and his forces are conducting an emergency retrieval inside a Koopa King's castle
The forty witnesses — former Royal Scribe confirmed the handwriting in public; forty people heard the core facts; the Regency could burn the journal but could not burn forty memories

Molly, Gus, and Vance — three civilians who agreed to help because they had sisters who worked in Peach's kitchens, because they had spent twenty years reading lava flows, because they had opinions about the Mages' Guild; ordinary people who made the escape possible
The tunnel collapse — designed to make Bowser too visible to quietly eliminate, not to start a war; worked well enough to buy time and badly enough to redirect a lava tube
The debrief's completeness — reads like documentation written by someone who expected to become unavailable and made himself a complete source so that unavailability would not mean information lost
Toadsmith did not return with the others — Molly, Gus, and Vance came back to Donut Plains; Toadsmith did not; the gap between his filing the debrief and his disappearance is undocumented

The unsigned intelligence note — received by Waluigi eighty-five years later, nine days after Captain Toadette seized Toad Town; someone held this for eighty-five years and chose the moment the Regency's narrative began cracking to release it
Roses that grow in winter — Bloomia's encoded location; she knows the name in the third column; Waluigi has theories
openThreads: The engineer's identity — the operational fingerprint is consistent across the journal entries, the hooded figure footage, and the helicopter forces; the reader has sufficient information to form a conclusion; Waluigi will not write the name here

The silver key — delivered by the engineer to Peach approximately two weeks before the assassination; function undocumented in any recovered record; presumably carried by Bloomia in the leather case; what it opens is unknown

The journal's chain of custody — from the Donut Plains elder through eighty-five years to present day; the elder is almost certainly dead; whether the physical document survived is unknown; Waluigi intends to pursue this thread

Toadsmith's fate — most likely voluntary disappearance based on debrief completeness; less likely capture; least likely tunnel casualty; Waluigi holds the first assessment; the gap between the debrief filing and his failure to return with the others is the undocumented period

The blade's manufacturing chain — who inside the Guild had access to Koopa weapon fabrication techniques or Koopa supply networks; the blade was genuine Koopa-forged, meaning someone with real connections sourced it
The name in the third column — someone Peach loved enough to choose as her executioner; Bloomia knows; Bloomia has not spoken it
Bloomia's location — roses that grow in winter; Waluigi has theories and intends to test them

The SOS signal — whether it was intercepted by Eggman's forces monitoring Regency emergency frequencies, or whether Eggman's operation was already in motion independently; both versions of events are significant in different ways

The thirty-year enemy — Peach told the engineer the enemy had been in the room with him every day for thirty years; thirty years places this at the beginning of the institutional infrastructure that enabled the conspiracy; the enemy was always there, invisible as furniture
The unsigned intelligence note — who held this information since 955 BF, why they chose to release it nine days after Captain Toadette seized Toad Town, and what they expect Waluigi to do with it

Whether the counter-conspiracy is succeeding — Peach designed her death to eventually expose the conspirators; eighty-five years later the narrative is cracking; people are releasing secrets they held for decades; the structure is failing; whether this is the outcome she planned for or something she could not have anticipated is the question Waluigi cannot answer yet
